title: Introduction to Supervised Learning knowledge check

questions.prompt: Which statement best captures the central idea of “Introduction to Supervised Learning”?
options: Introduction to Supervised Learning focuses on Labeled datasets; Inputs and target outputs; Training objectives. Define the terms used in the lesson, identify the assumptions that connect the inputs to the result, and use a small example to check whether the chosen approach fits the stated goal. Supervised learning maps input features to known targets. Match the problem type and...
It guarantees correct outcomes in every context and removes the need for independent evaluation.
It is always identical to a fixed if/then script, regardless of the data or task.
It can be trusted solely because its output is fluent or its internal score is high.
questions.answer_key: Introduction to Supervised Learning focuses on Labeled datasets; Inputs and target outputs; Training objectives. Define the terms used in the lesson, identify the assumptions that connect the inputs to the result, and use a small example to check whether the chosen approach fits the stated goal. Supervised learning maps input features to known targets. Match the problem type and...
questions.explanation: The lesson defines the topic this way: Introduction to Supervised Learning focuses on Labeled datasets; Inputs and target outputs; Training objectives. Define the terms used in the lesson, identify the assumptions that connect the inputs to the result, and use a small example to check whether the chosen approach fits the stated goal. Supervised learning maps input features to known targets. Match the problem type and... The distractors claim guarantees or equivalences that are not supported by the curriculum.

questions.prompt: When applying “Introduction to Supervised Learning” to a new problem, which practice is the strongest default?
options: Skip evaluation when the first demonstration looks convincing.
Use a small, representative test set, compare against an explicit baseline, inspect errors, and document assumptions.
Tune all decisions directly on the final test examples until the score improves.
Assume a method that worked once will work on every population and input distribution.
questions.answer_key: Use a small, representative test set, compare against an explicit baseline, inspect errors, and document assumptions.
questions.explanation: Use a small, representative test set, compare against an explicit baseline, inspect errors, and document assumptions. This practice makes assumptions visible and gives a reviewer evidence beyond one convincing demonstration.

questions.prompt: Which conclusion is appropriately cautious after a system demonstrates “Introduction to Supervised Learning”?
options: The system has proven its result is unbiased and safe for every use.
A successful example removes the need for monitoring or documentation.
No. Check uncertainty, context, data quality, security, and affected users; report limitations and use human oversight appropriate to the impact.
Any numeric score or generated explanation is a guarantee of factual correctness.
questions.answer_key: No. Check uncertainty, context, data quality, security, and affected users; report limitations and use human oversight appropriate to the impact.
questions.explanation: Observed performance is conditional on the test conditions. Review uncertainty, context, risks, and failures before deciding how the system may be used.
